Hi, I'm Kelly, and I have groomed dogs in St. Augustine for twelve years. Border collies have a lot of hair, so bath day takes time. First, the dog is brushed for about ten minutes, because a wet knot is very hard to remove. Then, the dog is washed with warm water and a gentle shampoo. After that, the dog is dried with a big towel and then with a dryer, for about thirty minutes. While the dog is drying, I check the ears and the paws. Finally, the nails are cut. Most dogs hate this step, so I always give them a treat at the end.

My name is Frank, and my family grows datil peppers just outside St. Augustine. The peppers are picked early in the morning, before the sun gets too hot. Then, they are sorted by color: green, yellow and orange. After that, the best peppers are put in small boxes, and the others are used for our own sauce. Finally, on Saturday, the boxes are taken to the farmers market downtown, and they are sold in about two hours. People come from Jacksonville and even from Orlando to buy them.
